source_quality.notes: Twenty-five pages. Empty text layers on pages 2, 9, 16, and 21 were opened as rasters. Equation 1, equations 4 through 6, equations 7 through 10, equation 12, and equation 15 were read from crops because the text layer dropped hats, roots, or whole lines. Watermark blocks were not paired into tables.

task_reconstruction.summary: Predict 2028 gold and total medals, give intervals, and name countries that rise or fall.
Name countries with no medal yet that may win one in 2028.
Relate events to medals and judge the host's new events.
Estimate a great-coach effect and pick three countries.

section_map.summary: Summary sheet with four In Task blocks and a keyword line.
Four assumptions, a notation table, and the start of cleaning.
The stacked prediction and the 2028 table.
Pearson r and the start of SHAP.
Three DID columns and the 3.213 reading.
A letter to national committees, then references.

contributions.summary: A four-learner stack, written as a linear sum, reaches R2 0.88.
Five first-medal countries are listed with accuracies from 88.32 down to 73.15.
A coach coefficient of 3.213 is the fully controlled specification.

dependency_graph.summary: Base-learner outputs become the inputs of equation (6).
SHAP is applied to the medal model rather than to a new regressor.
SMD is the check on the match behind the coach coefficient.

assumptions.summary: Merging historical sub-teams does not change measured national strength.
Coaching effects stay stable across a career.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Duplicate sport names are merged. Russia and ROC are kept out of the forecast.
Lagged medals, host status, and athlete counts are the constructed features.

models.summary: Stacking combines LightGBM, SVM, XGBoost, and a random forest.
Bootstrap percentiles supply the 95 percent intervals.
Pearson r and a Shapley value rank sports.

verification.summary: Stacking leads the five-model metric table on R2, MSE, and MAPE.
Three DID specifications are printed, and the prose prefers the third.
Ten-fold averages sit close to the single split, and SMD is 0.0013.

results_trace.summary: The United States, Australia, and France rise. China, Japan, and the Netherlands fall.
Mali leads the first-medal list at 88.32 percent.
Spain, Japan, and Canada are the three coach investments, at 4.32, 2.89, and 4.75.

writing_logic.summary: Each summary block starts with In Task N, then one model, then one number.
A metric is given a job, and the next equation label is glued to the period.
The close is a letter, with should for leaders and can for the others.

language_observations.summary: In Task N colon, then We, then one score in a which-clause.
A heatmap sentence is repeated with growth changed to increase.
Equation 14 is the lead-in of display (13) and of display (14).

visualization_observations.summary: The contents run from Introduction to Letter. There is no strengths section and no references line.
Figure 1 is the work map promised by the as-follows sentence. The text layer does not transcribe its boxes.
Figure 2 groups lagged medals, host status, and athlete counts. The caption spells Fearture.
Figure 3 is the stacking diagram: four learners, two training-set boxes.
Figure 4 is the 2028 medal table. USA 56, 41, 36, 133. China 33, 30, 27, 90. Australia 25, 20, 28, 73.
Figure 5 is the metric table. Stacking is 0.88, 0.32, 0.30.
Figure 6 prints 95 percent intervals. Headers are Sliver and Brozen. USA gold is 52-57.
Figure 7 is the never-medaled country chart. The later caption points at a red fitted line in this figure.
Figure 8 is the participation-trend chart for the top 28 non-medal countries.
Figure 9 links sports to first medals. Figure 10 lists MLI, SLE, BOL, HON, and GBS with accuracies.
Figure 11 is the sport-by-medal correlation heatmap.
Figure 12 is the five-step SHAP chevron.
Figure 13 ranks SHAP values for the United States, China, and Australia.
Figure 14 is the PSM-DID flowchart, with Logist and matehed samples.
Figure 15 compares propensity-score densities before and after matching.
Table 2 reports three DID specifications. Column 3 is 3.213 at p 0.02.
Figure 16 is the medal path around Karolyi's arrival. Figure 17 is the K-means step chart.
Figure 18 plots women's gymnastics medals against participation. Spain, Japan, and Canada are the named countries.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A judge can check that 0.88 is the largest R2 in the five-model row.
A judge can check that the USA gold point 56 is outside the interval 52-57.
A judge can check that 3.213 is column 3 and that column 2 is 1.53.

weaknesses.summary: The headline gold point sits outside its own interval.
The correlation sentence is printed twice.
A p-value of 0.02 is printed with no stars, and one cell is a dash.
The promised strengths section is a letter, and the letter adds a country.

independent_extensions.summary: The three DID columns could be discussed as a specification path, without changing 3.213 or 1.53.

unresolved_questions: Figure 1 box text was not cropped. The as-follows sentence is the source for the roadmap.
Figure 7 and Figure 8 were not cropped. The red-line sentence is the text source.
Figure 11 cell values were not read. The summary says above 0.6 and the page says higher.
Figure 13 bar values were not read. The country sports come from the prose.
The bootstrap count B is not stated.
The SMD of 0.0013 is not tied to a named covariate.
